description:
FILED s419 (Fable) by the flip re-census (docs/drop-census-s419-flip-gate.md
family 12).  3 drops, reason `PCL internal: no form emitter for expression
leaf PPI::Token::Number:?`:

  op/postfixderef.t:354 (+ perl-tests/postfixderef.t:354)
      bless [ "$_[$_[2]]"." plus "."$_[!$_[2]]" ]
  op/numconvert.t:200
      my $diag = "'$ans[0]' ne '$ans[1]',\t$num\t=> @opnames[$first,@{$curops[0]},$last] vs ...";

The `?` after `PPI::Token::Number:` is the leaf CONTENT the emitter printed â
i.e. an interpolated subscript containing `!` or a slice-with-block produced
a Number token whose content is not a number PCL can read (likely the
interpolation scanner mis-slicing the span, handing PExpr a fragment).
DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT first: transpile `my @x=(1,2); my @i=(0,1);
print "$x[!$i[0]]";` and dump what InterpScan hands the fragment parser.
If the span is mis-sliced this is an InterpScan bug (docs/interp-scan.md);
if the span is right it is a fragment-parse gap.  Blocks the announce->DIE
flip.

DONE s420.  Not an InterpScan span bug: the fragment parsers in
StringInterpolation CLONED the top-level parts of their mini-document but
nothing held the clones, and PPI's DESTROY empties every descendant — so a
clone that is a NODE (the inner `[0]` of "$x[$i[0]]") took its own tokens down
with it and the leaf emitter died on `content` = undef.  The `:?` in the
message was that undef.  Fix: one _anchor helper, used at all six clone sites.
Affects every nested interpolated subscript, not just the census rows:
"$x[$i[0]]", "$x[$h{k}]", "$x[!$i[0]]", "@ops[$first,@{$cur[0]},$last]".
3 census drops -> 0; perl-tests/postfixderef.t test 107 (concat overloading)
now passes — TOTAL passing 18363 -> 18364.  Guards: 2 rows in
Pl/t/interp-chained-subscript-01.t.
title: Interpolation dies 'no form emitter for expression leaf PPI::Token::Number:?' on $_[!$_[2]]-style subscripts (3 drops)
